messages:
nina: FYI running into a tricky SDK behavior in the async sample-app when customers combine a corporate forward proxy + custom CA + ALPINE-based docker runner. The async client falls back to the public API and retries infinitely (well, until our httpx max retries) and the cert chain fails on the runner only. Repro below.

nina: envs i set (in dockerfile):
  REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://dedicated-eu.internal
  REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA=/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem
  HTTP_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:8080
  REDWOOD_USE_PROXY=true

nina: command: 
  python -m asyncio run sample_app_async.py

nina: sample snippet:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # expect env-based base_url + custom CA
await client.responses.create(input="hi")
```

nina: error (trimmed):
```
httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Too many open connections
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx.ConnectError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/responses (Caused by SSLError("certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate"))
```

paul: interesting that alpine only. musl's cert store and CA bundle paths differ. do you see the file at /etc/ssl/certs/company.pem inside the container? maybe update CA_CERT_BUNDLE env?

nina: checked — file exists. sync client (redwood.Client) in same container works fine. Only AsyncClient trips.

ashley: likely two separate problems: (1) httpx's AsyncHTTPTransport is not inheriting our REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA when REDWOOD_USE_PROXY=true (similar to earlier reports), (2) our retry logic in async path reconstructs absolute URL when proxying and accidentally substitutes the host with the public default if base_url wasn't canonicalized early. That triggers retries to public host and then SSL mismatch.

paul: confirm: we set REDWOOD_USE_PROXY to gate proxy behavior, but AsyncClient init sometimes reads HTTP_PROXY from env directly and skips base_url resolution. Could be a race in config precedence. The fix should be deterministic: explicit constructor args > REDWOOD_* env > HTTP_PROXY heuristics.

nina: workaround that worked for me in the container: explicitly pass base_url and ssl context into AsyncClient: 
```py
import ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
sslctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://dedicated-eu.internal', _transport_kwargs={'ssl_context': sslctx, 'proxies': {"https": "http://corp-proxy:8080"}})
```

ashley: thanks — two quick notes for the PR: (A) avoid private/non-public kwarg names like _transport_kwargs in public API; instead provide transport_kwargs typed mapping on AsyncClient.__init__ (B) add an integration test that runs on alpine runner matrix to catch musl CA path regressions.

nina: opened issue #6128 documenting the alpine CI flake + workaround.

paul: i'll draft a small fix: (1) set httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=explicit_or_env) unconditionally at init, (2) construct ssl.SSLContext from REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA and pass into AsyncHTTPTransport even when proxy is present, (3) update retry/backoff wrapper to use request.url.with_host(base_url.host) rather than reconstructing naive absolute URLs. Will push PR shortly and tag eng/devex.

ashley: typing: mypy showed AsyncClient.__init__ signature mismatch because our stub in stubs/async.pyi didn't include transport/ssl args. add overloads and document in CHANGELOG.

devex-bot: created PR #4399: async/httpx: propagate custom CA + fix base_url precedence + alpine integration test (draft).

ci-bot: ci/sample-app: linux-integ ✅, alpine-integ ❌ (ssl verify failed) — triggering rebuild logs.

nina: thanks, i'll re-run alpine after the PR updates. leaving a note in sample-app/README about explicit base_url in containerized proxy envs until this lands. :+1:

paul: great teamwork — let's also add a tiny comment in sdk/CONFIG.md about env precedence so customers understand why passing base_url in code is safest in proxied CI images.
